measurements.name: Transmission line proximity

measurements.name: On-site generation potential
measurements.question: Can the site self-supply or bridge with on-site generation?
measurements.notes: Composite: gas pipeline 24.58 km (65% weight), GHI 5.45 kWh/m2/day (35% weight). Wind and land-for-generation components not yet implemented — index is therefore conservative. Solar/wind cannot firm a data center load; counted here only for a hybrid or bridging strategy.

measurements.name: Wet-bulb temperature profile
measurements.question: How many hours per year exceed the free-cooling wet-bulb threshold?
measurements.notes: Design wet-bulb (0.4% exceedance) 27.6 C; mean 21.4 C. Computed from 10 yr of ERA5 hourly reanalysis via Stull (2011).

measurements.name: Dry-bulb temperature profile and free-cooling hours
measurements.question: How many hours per year permit free (economizer) cooling?
measurements.notes: 2275 h/yr below 24.0 C. Design dry-bulb 38.1 C. Indicative PUE 1.263 — a screening proxy, not a CFD-grade model.

measurements.name: Extreme heat trend to 2050
measurements.question: How much does design-day temperature rise over the asset life?
measurements.notes: MODELED, NOT PROJECTED: linear extrapolation of the observed 30-year trend in annual design-day temperature (+0.040 C/yr). This is a placeholder for NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 and should not be cited as a climate projection.

measurements.name: Terrain slope
measurements.question: Mean and 90th-percentile slope across the developable area.
measurements.notes: mapzen DEM, 5x5 grid over 2.0 km. Mean slope 0.5%, p90 0.8%, relief 19 m. Below 2% is essentially free; earthwork cost rises roughly quadratically above that for a large flat-pad campus.

measurements.name: Contiguous developable area
measurements.question: Largest contiguous buildable area available at the site.
measurements.notes: SCREENING ESTIMATE ONLY. rural with settlement (27 buildings/km2) within 5.0 km; assumed 53% developable. This is an upper bound on physically developable land and a much looser upper bound on ACQUIRABLE land — parcel fragmentation typically cuts it by half or more. Confirm against cadastral data before any decision.

measurements.name: Brownfield and retired-asset opportunity

measurements.notes: 14 industrial land parcel(s) nearby.

measurements.name: Internet exchange and cloud on-ramp proximity

measurements.notes: Nearest interconnection facility 'Ishan Technologies Rajkot' at 77.6 km; 1 facilities within 100 km. Weight this near zero for a training campus — over-weighting it biases site selection toward expensive metro land.

measurements.name: Transmission line proximity
measurements.question: Distance to the nearest transmission line of sufficient voltage to serve target load.
measurements.notes: 230 kV line at 4.0 km; 393 line(s) at or above 230 kV within 60 km. Proximity is not capacity — read with pwr.substation_headroom.

measurements.name: On-site generation potential
measurements.question: Can the site self-supply or bridge with on-site generation?
measurements.notes: Composite: gas pipeline not found km, GHI 4.27 kWh/m2/day (35% weight). Wind and land-for-generation components not yet implemented — index is therefore conservative. Solar/wind cannot firm a data center load; counted here only for a hybrid or bridging strategy.

measurements.name: Wet-bulb temperature profile
measurements.question: How many hours per year exceed the free-cooling wet-bulb threshold?
measurements.notes: Design wet-bulb (0.4% exceedance) 25.6 C; mean 11.7 C. Computed from 10 yr of ERA5 hourly reanalysis via Stull (2011).

measurements.name: Reclaimed water availability
measurements.question: Is treated effluent available at sufficient volume and acceptable distance?
measurements.notes: Distance only — treated flow capacity must be confirmed with the operator. Reclaimed water is usually the highest score-per-dollar water intervention available: it neutralizes most community opposition and is often cheaper than potable.

measurements.name: Dry-bulb temperature profile and free-cooling hours
measurements.question: How many hours per year permit free (economizer) cooling?
measurements.notes: 6991 h/yr below 24.0 C. Design dry-bulb 35.1 C. Indicative PUE 1.145 — a screening proxy, not a CFD-grade model.

measurements.name: Extreme heat trend to 2050
measurements.question: How much does design-day temperature rise over the asset life?
measurements.notes: MODELED, NOT PROJECTED: linear extrapolation of the observed 30-year trend in annual design-day temperature (+0.062 C/yr). This is a placeholder for NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 and should not be cited as a climate projection.

measurements.name: Riverine and pluvial flood exposure
measurements.question: Does the site intersect a modeled flood zone, and at what return period?
measurements.notes: Outside mapped FEMA flood hazard areas. Note that NFHL does not model pluvial (flash) flooding, which no widely-available dataset captures well — this is a known blind spot, not a clean bill of health.

measurements.name: Terrain slope
measurements.question: Mean and 90th-percentile slope across the developable area.
measurements.notes: mapzen DEM, 5x5 grid over 2.0 km. Mean slope 0.8%, p90 1.5%, relief 25 m. Below 2% is essentially free; earthwork cost rises roughly quadratically above that for a large flat-pad campus.

measurements.name: Contiguous developable area
measurements.question: Largest contiguous buildable area available at the site.
measurements.notes: SCREENING ESTIMATE ONLY. exurban / village (108 buildings/km2) within 5.0 km; assumed 33% developable. This is an upper bound on physically developable land and a much looser upper bound on ACQUIRABLE land — parcel fragmentation typically cuts it by half or more. Confirm against cadastral data before any decision.

measurements.name: Internet exchange and cloud on-ramp proximity
measurements.question: Network distance to the nearest significant IXP or cloud on-ramp.
measurements.notes: Nearest interconnection facility 'Pixel Factory Data Center' at 7.9 km; 7 facilities within 100 km. Weight this near zero for a training campus — over-weighting it biases site selection toward expensive metro land.

measurements.name: Carrier availability
measurements.question: How many distinct network operators can deliver service on site?
measurements.notes: 38 network presences across 6 facilities within 50 km. Network presences at carrier-neutral facilities are a proxy for carrier availability, not a direct count of carriers able to serve this parcel.

measurements.name: Long-haul fiber proximity
measurements.question: Distance to the nearest long-haul fiber route.
measurements.notes: INFERRED, NOT MEASURED: no fiber routes mapped; distance is to the nearest telecom exchange or data center, used as a proxy for route presence. Tier D.

measurements.name: Residential proximity and noise exposure
measurements.question: How many residences fall within the noise-relevant buffer?
measurements.notes: 0 estimated dwellings from 0 OSM residential features within 1.0 km. Apartment blocks estimated at 4 units/level. Noise from chillers and generator testing is the most common specific complaint in data center opposition — distance is the cheapest mitigation. Zero count may reflect sparse OSM building coverage rather than genuinely empty land; tier lowered to C.

measurements.name: Port and rail access
measurements.question: Can heavy imported equipment reach the site efficiently?
measurements.notes: Read together with lnd.heavy_haul_access: a nearby port is worthless if the final approach cannot carry a 300-tonne transformer. OSM port tagging is inconsistent; treat as screening-grade.

measurements.name: Organized opposition risk
measurements.question: Is there active, organized opposition to data centers in this jurisdiction?
measurements.notes: Hanover County Board of Supervisors approved the 1,200-acre Tract rezoning UNANIMOUSLY on 27 Mar 2024, after a unanimous Planning Commission recommendation in January. A unanimous vote is the strongest available signal of local political appetite.

measurements.name: Zoning and entitlement status
measurements.question: Is the current zoning compatible, and if not, how hard is the path?
measurements.notes: Required discretionary rezoning, which carries political risk in principle — but it passed unanimously at both commission and board, so the pathway was routine in practice for this jurisdiction at that time.

measurements.name: Land acquisition cost
measurements.question: Expected all-in acquisition cost per hectare.
measurements.notes: Actual transaction: $33M for 1,200 acres (May 2024) = ~$27,500/ha. This is a real arms-length sale price post-entitlement, not a comparable — unusually good evidence for this factor, though still Tier C since it was read from press coverage rather than a parsed deed record.

measurements.name: Accelerator export control exposure
measurements.question: Can the intended compute legally be installed and operated here?
measurements.notes: US domestic deployment. Advanced accelerators may be installed and operated at a US site without export licensing; the controls govern export and re-export, not domestic use. Rule set checked 2026-09-03 — this is the fastest-moving input in the framework and must be re-verified per analysis.

measurements.name: Transmission line proximity
measurements.question: Distance to the nearest transmission line of sufficient voltage to serve target load.
measurements.notes: 400 kV line at 5.3 km; 136 line(s) at or above 230 kV within 60 km. Proximity is not capacity — read with pwr.substation_headroom.

measurements.name: On-site generation potential
measurements.question: Can the site self-supply or bridge with on-site generation?
measurements.notes: Composite: gas pipeline not found km, GHI 5.16 kWh/m2/day (35% weight). Wind and land-for-generation components not yet implemented — index is therefore conservative. Solar/wind cannot firm a data center load; counted here only for a hybrid or bridging strategy.

measurements.name: Wet-bulb temperature profile
measurements.question: How many hours per year exceed the free-cooling wet-bulb threshold?
measurements.notes: Design wet-bulb (0.4% exceedance) 27.5 C; mean 22.5 C. Computed from 10 yr of ERA5 hourly reanalysis via Stull (2011).

measurements.name: Reclaimed water availability
measurements.question: Is treated effluent available at sufficient volume and acceptable distance?
measurements.notes: Distance only — treated flow capacity must be confirmed with the operator. Reclaimed water is usually the highest score-per-dollar water intervention available: it neutralizes most community opposition and is often cheaper than potable.

measurements.name: Dry-bulb temperature profile and free-cooling hours
measurements.question: How many hours per year permit free (economizer) cooling?
measurements.notes: 1498 h/yr below 24.0 C. Design dry-bulb 39.6 C. Indicative PUE 1.282 — a screening proxy, not a CFD-grade model.

measurements.name: Extreme heat trend to 2050
measurements.question: How much does design-day temperature rise over the asset life?
measurements.notes: MODELED, NOT PROJECTED: linear extrapolation of the observed 30-year trend in annual design-day temperature (+0.140 C/yr). This is a placeholder for NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 and should not be cited as a climate projection.

measurements.name: Terrain slope
measurements.question: Mean and 90th-percentile slope across the developable area.
measurements.notes: mapzen DEM, 5x5 grid over 2.0 km. Mean slope 0.5%, p90 0.8%, relief 37 m. Below 2% is essentially free; earthwork cost rises roughly quadratically above that for a large flat-pad campus.

measurements.name: Contiguous developable area
measurements.question: Largest contiguous buildable area available at the site.
measurements.notes: SCREENING ESTIMATE ONLY. suburban (271 buildings/km2) within 5.0 km; assumed 16% developable. This is an upper bound on physically developable land and a much looser upper bound on ACQUIRABLE land — parcel fragmentation typically cuts it by half or more. Confirm against cadastral data before any decision.

measurements.name: Brownfield and retired-asset opportunity
measurements.question: Is this a retired industrial or generation site with reusable infrastructure?
measurements.notes: 67 industrial land parcel(s) nearby.

measurements.name: Internet exchange and cloud on-ramp proximity
measurements.question: Network distance to the nearest significant IXP or cloud on-ramp.
measurements.notes: Nearest interconnection facility 'Nxtra Data Mumbai DC 3' at 2.1 km; 53 facilities within 100 km. Weight this near zero for a training campus — over-weighting it biases site selection toward expensive metro land.

measurements.name: Carrier availability
measurements.question: How many distinct network operators can deliver service on site?
measurements.notes: 936 network presences across 49 facilities within 50 km. Network presences at carrier-neutral facilities are a proxy for carrier availability, not a direct count of carriers able to serve this parcel.

measurements.name: Long-haul fiber proximity
measurements.question: Distance to the nearest long-haul fiber route.
measurements.notes: OSM telecom route coverage is sparse and inconsistent worldwide. Tier C even when a route is found. Confirm with carriers or a paid route dataset.

measurements.name: Residential proximity and noise exposure
measurements.question: How many residences fall within the noise-relevant buffer?
measurements.notes: 214 estimated dwellings from 26 OSM residential features within 1.0 km. Apartment blocks estimated at 4 units/level. Noise from chillers and generator testing is the most common specific complaint in data center opposition — distance is the cheapest mitigation.

queue.question: How much spare capacity (MVA) exists at the nearest suitable substation?
queue.artifact: Load-serving study or written statement of available capacity at the named substation, for the named load, in the named year.
queue.note: The single most common cause of a project dying after twelve months of work. Nothing published substitutes for the utility saying it in writing.

queue.question: Realistic years from application to energization for target load.
queue.owner: ISO/RTO interconnection queue, then the utility
queue.artifact: Queue position and cluster study schedule for a comparable request

queue.question: What fraction of available renewable supply is already withdrawn in this basin?
queue.artifact: Will-serve letter or withdrawal permit precedent

queue.question: How hard is it to obtain the legal right to the required volume?
queue.artifact: Permit precedent for comparable industrial withdrawal in the same basin

queue.question: Storm surge and 2050 sea level rise exposure.
queue.artifact: Site-specific study; global rasters are screening-grade only

queue.question: Largest contiguous buildable area available at the site.
queue.artifact: ALTA survey or local equivalent showing contiguous developable acreage

queue.question: Does the site intersect protected areas, wetlands, or critical habitat?
queue.artifact: Zoning determination letter and title/survey

queue.question: All-in modeled cost per kW-year across power, land, construction, tax and ops.
queue.artifact: 10-year TCO model built on the confirmed tariff, land price and scope
queue.note: Depends on the tariff, land price and incentive answers above. It cannot be credibly modeled before them, which is why it is usually last in the queue and first in the investment memo.

gates.name: Credible power path to target load
gates.reason: Substation available capacity is unknown — the most common cause of late-stage project failure. Verify with the utility before committing capital.

gates.name: Water viability for the assumed cooling architecture
gates.reason: Water availability and rights both unmeasured.

gates.name: Flood exclusion
gates.reason: Outside the 500-year floodplain (modeled return period 1000 yr).

gates.name: Entitlement path exists
gates.reason: Requires discretionary rezoning (rezoning_contested) — this converts an engineering problem into a political one.

gates.name: No active data center moratorium
gates.reason: Organized local opposition is present and has defeated or delayed comparable applications.

measurements.name: Transmission line proximity
measurements.question: Distance to the nearest transmission line of sufficient voltage to serve target load.
measurements.notes: 230 kV line at 2.7 km; 392 line(s) at or above 230 kV within 60 km. Proximity is not capacity — read with pwr.substation_headroom.

measurements.name: On-site generation potential
measurements.question: Can the site self-supply or bridge with on-site generation?
measurements.notes: Composite: gas pipeline not found km, GHI 4.27 kWh/m2/day (35% weight). Wind and land-for-generation components not yet implemented — index is therefore conservative. Solar/wind cannot firm a data center load; counted here only for a hybrid or bridging strategy.

measurements.name: Wet-bulb temperature profile
measurements.question: How many hours per year exceed the free-cooling wet-bulb threshold?
measurements.notes: Design wet-bulb (0.4% exceedance) 25.6 C; mean 11.7 C. Computed from 10 yr of ERA5 hourly reanalysis via Stull (2011).

measurements.name: Dry-bulb temperature profile and free-cooling hours
measurements.question: How many hours per year permit free (economizer) cooling?
measurements.notes: 6941 h/yr below 24.0 C. Design dry-bulb 35.5 C. Indicative PUE 1.146 — a screening proxy, not a CFD-grade model.

measurements.name: Extreme heat trend to 2050
measurements.question: How much does design-day temperature rise over the asset life?
measurements.notes: MODELED, NOT PROJECTED: linear extrapolation of the observed 30-year trend in annual design-day temperature (+0.070 C/yr). This is a placeholder for NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 and should not be cited as a climate projection.

measurements.name: Riverine and pluvial flood exposure
measurements.question: Does the site intersect a modeled flood zone, and at what return period?
measurements.notes: Outside mapped FEMA flood hazard areas. Note that NFHL does not model pluvial (flash) flooding, which no widely-available dataset captures well — this is a known blind spot, not a clean bill of health.

measurements.name: Terrain slope
measurements.question: Mean and 90th-percentile slope across the developable area.
measurements.notes: mapzen DEM, 5x5 grid over 2.0 km. Mean slope 1.0%, p90 1.6%, relief 30 m. Below 2% is essentially free; earthwork cost rises roughly quadratically above that for a large flat-pad campus.

measurements.name: Brownfield and retired-asset opportunity
measurements.question: Is this a retired industrial or generation site with reusable infrastructure?
measurements.notes: 1 power plant(s) within 8 km; nearest Henrico Power Plant (biogas) at 2.31 km. CHECK RETIREMENT STATUS — a retiring plant is the highest-value site category available, because interconnection rights, transmission, water rights and often the land itself are already in place.

measurements.name: Internet exchange and cloud on-ramp proximity
measurements.question: Network distance to the nearest significant IXP or cloud on-ramp.
measurements.notes: Nearest interconnection facility 'EdgeConneX Richmond (EDCRIC01)' at 8.6 km; 7 facilities within 100 km. Weight this near zero for a training campus — over-weighting it biases site selection toward expensive metro land.

measurements.name: Carrier availability
measurements.question: How many distinct network operators can deliver service on site?
measurements.notes: 38 network presences across 6 facilities within 50 km. Network presences at carrier-neutral facilities are a proxy for carrier availability, not a direct count of carriers able to serve this parcel.

measurements.name: Residential proximity and noise exposure
measurements.question: How many residences fall within the noise-relevant buffer?
measurements.notes: 37 estimated dwellings from 4 OSM residential features within 1.0 km. Apartment blocks estimated at 4 units/level. Noise from chillers and generator testing is the most common specific complaint in data center opposition — distance is the cheapest mitigation.

measurements.name: Port and rail access
measurements.question: Can heavy imported equipment reach the site efficiently?
measurements.notes: Read together with lnd.heavy_haul_access: a nearby port is worthless if the final approach cannot carry a 300-tonne transformer. OSM port tagging is inconsistent; treat as screening-grade.

measurements.name: Organized opposition risk
measurements.question: Is there active, organized opposition to data centers in this jurisdiction?
measurements.notes: Hanover County Board of Supervisors REJECTED the 430-acre Mountain Road Technology Park 4-3 in May 2026 after months of organized resident opposition on water use, environment, traffic and noise. A split denial against mobilized residents is the strongest negative signal this factor captures.

measurements.name: Zoning and entitlement status
measurements.question: Is the current zoning compatible, and if not, how hard is the path?
measurements.notes: Required both a conditional use permit and rezoning; both were denied. The entitlement pathway is demonstrably contested in this specific corridor, as distinct from the same county's Beaverdam district where the same developer was approved unanimously.

measurements.name: Accelerator export control exposure
measurements.question: Can the intended compute legally be installed and operated here?
measurements.notes: US domestic deployment. Advanced accelerators may be installed and operated at a US site without export licensing; the controls govern export and re-export, not domestic use. Rule set checked 2026-09-03 — this is the fastest-moving input in the framework and must be re-verified per analysis.

hyperscale_training.label: Hyperscale AI training campus
hyperscale_training.description: Large-scale model training. Latency-insensitive, power-dominated, needs enormous contiguous land and a multi-hundred-megawatt power path. This is the profile most 2025-2030 AI capex targets.

inference_edge.label: Inference and edge serving
inference_edge.description: User-facing inference. Latency-critical, modest power, must be near demand. Land and power price matter far less; connectivity and metro proximity dominate.

retrofit_colo.label: Retrofit / colocation conversion
retrofit_colo.description: Converting existing industrial shells or upgrading legacy colo to AI-capable density. Constrained by existing structure, floor loading, and power feed.
